Find the area between the curve $y=-2{x}^{2}-x+3$, the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, shown above.
worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-2{x}^{2}-x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-1{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+3{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\cdot {\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}-1\cdot {\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{1}+3x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-2(\frac{1}{3}-0)-1(\frac{1}{2}-0)+3(1-0) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2}+3 \\  & =\frac{11}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
